Article 2. Major Offense. A student shall be subjected to disciplinary action ranging from deprivation of certain students’ privileges, suspension and expulsion if he commits serious deviations from the expected norm of behavior as an LSPU student. The following acts are strictly prohibited.

Sec. 1. Acts of Cybercrime (Stipulated by RA 10175 or the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012).

1.1. Cyber bullying or bullying done through the use of technology or any electronic means
 1st Offense: Suspension for one (1) month
 2nd Offense: Suspension for one (1) semester
 3rd Offense: Expulsion from the University

1.2. Illegal access or hacking to the whole or any part of one’s online accounts including e -mail, social media profiles, etc.
 1st Offense: Suspension for one (1) month
 2nd Offense: Suspension for one (1) semester
 3rd Offense: Expulsion from the University

1.3. Illegal interception or listening to, recording, monitoring or surveillance of the content of communications, either directly through the access and use of computer systems, or indirectly through the use of electronic eavesdropping or tapping devices
 1st Offense: Suspension for one (1) month

SECTION: HOW TO REPORT BULLYING OR HARASSMENT (STEP-BY-STEP)
HOW TO REPORT BULLYING OR HARASSMENT (STEP-BY-STEP)
Source: reporting to the College Dean is from campus information supplied by the maintainer (September 2026). The written complaint to OSAS and the committee are from the Student Handbook, Chapter 6, Articles 2 and 6 (Anti-Bullying Act of 2013, RA 10627, is the legal basis of the bullying offenses). Steps 1 and 4 are practical advice.
Bullying or harassment must be reported to your College Dean so it is noted and can be solved quickly. Four steps:
Step 1: Write down what happened. Note who was involved, what happened, when and where, and who saw it. For online bullying, keep screenshots and links. Do this while the details are fresh; it makes the report faster to act on.
Step 2: Tell your College Dean. Report it as soon as possible. The Dean notes the case and acts on it quickly at the college level; the Dean is also a member of the Student Discipline Committee for students of that college.
Step 3: File a signed written complaint with OSAS when formal action is needed. OSAS handles all complaints against alleged violators of the Code of Conduct.

 1st Offense: Suspension for one (1) week and 40 hours service to be rendered in the institution
 2nd Offense: Suspension for one (1) month

5.3. Unwanted physical contact between the bully and the victim like punching, pushing, etc. and the use of available objects as weapons
 1st Offense: Suspension for one (1) month

5.4. Any slanderous statement or accusation that causes the victim undue emotional distress like directing foul language or profanity at the target, name-calling, impersonating or calling/giving derogatory names etc.
 1st Offense: Suspension for one (1) month
 2nd Offense: Suspension for one (1) semester
